description: We are biotechnology engineering students from Arequipa, Peru, building TerraCrop to integrate climate, agricultural and Earth observation data to optimize crop rotation, water use and soil health. We seek collaborators in agriculture, Earth sciences, data analysis, programming and AI to create real-world impact.
summary:
In La Joya, Arequipa (Peru), most farmers decide what to plant and when based only on year of experience, without technical information about their soil, water or the climate ahead. In Peru, only 7.4% of farmers hace received training and only 3.7% have had technical assistance (INEI, National Agricultural Survey 2025). Without that information, every change becomes a loss: depleted soils, water shortages (in 2023 irrigation water in La Joya dropped by more than 45%) and climate events such as heat waves, frosts or El Niño.
TerraCrop is a smart crop planner; it takes the current state of a farm plor and projects it foward to what is coming. It has two functions. 
Analyzes the plot today. It combines NASA data (POWER, GPM and SMAP) low-cost sensors and an agronomic database of 14 local crops to recommend what to plant and in what sequence. When no crop can fix the soil problem, it recommends beneficial microorganisms.
Prepares the farmer for what is coming. It connects to official sources (ENFEN, SENAMHI and NOAA) that update daily or monthly, and turns each forecast into a specific action for the plot.
details:
What exactly does it do?

TerraCrop answers three questions farmers ask every seasons:

How is my plot doing? A traffic light (green, yellow and red) summarizes soil moisture, temperature, pH and salinity.

What should I plant in the time I have left? Suppose a farmer harvests garlin in August and plants it again in January. TerraCrop calculates that window of about 5 months and recommends a bridge crop that fits in that time, is compatible with garlic and corrects what the soil is missing. For example, beans inoculated with rhizobia if nitrogen is low.

What should I prepare for? If SENAMHI, Peru's national weather service, forecasts warmer nights, the app warns that onions may mature early and moves the next planting plan foward.

How Does It Work?

Plot registration: the farmer marks the plot on a map and enters the current crop and crop history

Diagnosis with NASA data and sensors: daily climate data from NASA POWER (2015-2025 and current) rainfall from GPM IMERG, soil moisture from SMAP, and hourly readings from ESP32 sensors (soil moisture, temperature, pH and electrical condictivity).

Estimated nutrient balance: sensors cannot measure nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium. TerraCrop therefore estimates the balance from what previous crops removed from the soil, using data from INIA (Peru's National Institute of Agrarian Innovation), and confirms it with a soil test when one is available.

SmartCycle, the rotation planner: it combines the real planting calendar of La Joya (crop stages recorded by SENAMHI), 196 crop compatibility rules and available water to propose planting sequences.

Biotechnology module: if no crop can correct the deficiency, it recommends the right microorganism: nitrogen-fixing bacteria, phosphorus-solubilizing bacteria, mycorrhizal fungi, biocontrol agents or salt-tolerant bacteria. It lists the available products registered with SENASA (Peru’s agricultural health authority) without promoting any brand, and shows which crops each product is registered for.

Early-warning alerts: every day it checks ENFEN official statements, SENAMHI warnings and bulletins, and NOAA’s ONI index. It compares them with each crop’s critical thresholds, including lethal frost temperatures, and sends alerts with a color, an icon and one clear action.

Scientific warnings: the app is honest about its limits. For example, it warns that a bridge crop restores nitrogen but does not eliminate white rot in garlic and onion.

Benefits

Data-driven decisions, not just intuition: science complements the farmer’s experience.

Prevention instead of losses: in 2024, heat shortened the onion cycle in Arequipa from 4 months to 3–3.5 months, and root fungi caused losses of 20–30%. TerraCrop warns ahead of time.

Healthier soils: crop rotations and beneficial microorganisms reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers.

Efficient water use: it prioritizes crops and growth stages based on available water.

Easy to use: four screens, icons and a traffic light, designed for farmers without technical training.

Replicable: it relies on open data and recommends microorganisms, not brands, so it can work in any valley with its own local sources and suppliers.

Intended Impact

TerraCrop brings technical assistance to farmers who currently have none. La Joya alone has about 10,000 farmers, according to local press. The project will be validated with La Joya farmers through a survey of their actual practices and pilot plots.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware and Software

Mobile app: Flutter (iOS and Android).

Data processing: Python and Google Earth Engine.

Agronomic database: Excel/JSON with 14 crops, the La Joya planting calendar, compatibility rules, critical thresholds, alerts and microorganisms.

Hardware: sensors connected to an ESP32 (soil moisture, temperature, pH, electrical conductivity).

Server: scheduled reading of official data sources.

NASA Data

NASA POWER: daily temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, solar radiation and wind (2015–2025 and current), used for climate diagnosis, anomaly detection and estimating each crop’s water needs.

GPM IMERG: precipitation.

SMAP L4: regional soil moisture.

Space Agency Partner and Other Data

NOAA CPC (Oceanic Niño Index), ENFEN (official El Niño statements), SENAMHI (crop stages observed at the MAP La Joya station, weather warnings and seasonal outlooks), INIA (garlic and onion fertilization manual for Arequipa; coastal agricultural calendar), INEI (National Agricultural Survey 2025), FAO-56 (crop water requirements), FAO-29 (salinity thresholds) and SENASA (registered biological inputs).

Use of Artificial Intelligence

  • Dart: User interfaces, navigation, maps, Smart-Cycle, store integration, crop recommendations, local storage, and testing frameworks.
  • Kotlin: Flutter-to-Android integration and build configuration management.
  • Swift: iOS integration, including application bootstrapping and native plugin registration.
  • JavaScript: Firebase cloud functions configured for dispatching critical alert notifications upon cloud deployment.
  • Python: Processing agricultural Excel spreadsheets and converting them into the application's underlying database.
  • HTML: Landing page for the web-based version of the project.
  • C++: Bootstrapping source files for the desktop editions (Windows and Linux) incorporated into the project
